title: Paisalo Digital Ltd - 532900 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Paisalo, a last-mile NBFC, posted record Q4 PAT of Rs.722 million (+56% YoY) and reaffirmed doubling AUM in three years, but there is no supply-side or capacity signal and the call is management-led with little hard data.

summary.headline: Paisalo posted record Q4 FY26 PAT of Rs.722 million, up 56% YoY, with AUM up 17% to Rs.61,009 million.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 35% YoY to Rs.2,609 million and net interest income rose 61% YoY to Rs.1,733 million, driving a record quarterly PAT. FY26 PAT was Rs.2,372 million, with total income up 22% and NII up 29%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 0.76% and NNPA at 0.61%, and cost of borrowing eased to 10.22%. Management reaffirmed a three-year guidance to double AUM, income and net profit, and said co-lending is excluded from that base.

financial_highlights.change: +3% QoQ as stated; management cited ~27% Q3 to Q4 growth

segments.name: Geography (Q4 AUM mix)
segments.commentary: Delhi 28.03%, Maharashtra 21.70% (+430 bps), Haryana 14.94%, Rajasthan 13.14%, Uttar Pradesh 14.12% (+122 bps), other states 8.07%.

segments.name: Sector (FY26 AUM mix)
segments.commentary: Food and hospitality 24%, Agri and allied agri 14%, street vendors 14%, heavy industries 11%, technology 8%, health and education 5%, textiles 4%, vehicles 3%, others 17%. MSME/SME 71%, income generation 29%.

segments.name: Distribution network
segments.commentary: 5,299 touchpoints across 22 states: 422 branches (up from 402, 20 added in Q4), 3,381 distribution points and 1,496 business correspondents; 427 touchpoints added in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Reaffirmed guidance to double AUM, AUM income and net profit over the next three fiscal years (FY27-FY29).
NIM to be maintained around 6.5% in FY27 versus 6.83% achieved in FY26; management hopes to overachieve.

Co-lending is excluded from the doubling target and treated as an addition on top; SBI co-lending: one arrangement expected live within Q1 FY27, the second awaiting the bank's RBI-compliance confirmation.

Six new lending segments (medical equipment, industrial equipment, alternative fuel, two-wheeler, agri-equipment, small commercial vehicles) with ~18-20 partnerships in Q4; plan to scale each in FY27.
capex_capacity: Branch network grew from 402 to 422 in Q4 FY26, with 20 branches added; total touchpoints 5,299 across 22 states.
Business correspondent partnership expanded with Indian Overseas Bank as part of banking-as-a-service platform.
AI-enabled pipelines processed ~1,60,000 loan applications in Q4; ~1,25,000 servicing cases and ~2,25,000 debt management cases handled by AI-assisted workflows; ~2,50,000 quality checks automated.
Outbound AI-led outreach of 1,50,000 calls, two live text bots and five outbound voice bots.
Headcount down 3% during FY26 despite branch expansion and double-digit AUM growth.
demand_pricing: Management described small-ticket credit demand as healthy and broad-based across micro-enterprises, informal segments and Tier 3-5 geographies.
Secured book: about 93% of portfolio secured per an analyst; management cited 50-60% LTV on secured cases, with recovery designed to cover principal and cost of funds, the loss being limited to NIM.

Middle East/Strait of Hormuz disruption affects large SMEs and mid-corporates with exports; management said it has no large concentrated exposure to export-dependent borrowers and expects LCC segment difficulty in the current quarter.
Management positioned Paisalo as not an MFI: it lends from the micro-enterprise stage onward, targeting an 8 lakh crore untapped market.

qa_highlights.question: Can NIM be sustained at current levels given higher loan yields and lower borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 NIM was 6.83%, above prior guidance, and it targets about 6.5% in FY27 while hoping to overachieve.

qa_highlights.question: What trends are seen in SME and overall book in April and May amid the war situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Stress is concentrated in large SMEs and mid-corporates with export exposure, hit by insurance, freight and Strait of Hormuz flow issues (about 5% capacity). Paisalo has no large concentrated exposure; LCC segment may see difficulty this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Update on co-lending expansion with State Bank of India?
qa_highlights.answer: Paisalo has completed its RBI-circular compliance on both methods; one is expected live within Q1 FY27 and the other awaits the bank's compliance confirmation, expected by end of Q1 or early Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How are NPAs recognised and what is recovery on collateral?
qa_highlights.answer: NPAs are recognised under RBI IRAC norms on both secured and unsecured books. Secured lending uses 50-60% LTV, with recovery typically covering principal plus cost of funds; only NIM is lost, not principal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the three-year doubling guidance still intact given the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management reaffirmed doubling AUM income and net profit over the next three fiscal years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters increase their stake this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters raised stake by about 4.7% last fiscal year after warrants of Rs.180 crore and 5% creeping acquisition earlier; management declined to comment on FY27 plans.

qa_highlights.question: How is collection efficiency at 98.5% achieved despite industry MFI stress, and is inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited a 'lend right, collect tight' philosophy with credit processes designed for elimination rather than servicing. It confirmed active scouting for inorganic opportunities and partners.

qa_highlights.question: Which new products will drive FY27 revenue, and why was QoQ disbursement growth low?
qa_highlights.answer: Six new segments have about 18-20 partnerships, to be scaled in FY27 with roughly three sub-products per category over time. Reported QoQ disbursement growth was 3%, with Q3 to Q4 growth of about 27% and FY26 growth about 15%.

risks_watch: Export-linked SME and mid-corporate stress from Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption; LCC segment may be affected in Q1 FY27.
Co-lending ramp-up depends on SBI completing RBI-circular compliance; timing slipped from earlier expectations and is not in the doubling base.
NIM guidance step-down from 6.83% to about 6.5% in FY27.
Execution of the three-year doubling target, including scaling the six new segments and the stated 8 new products.
Disclosure inconsistency: the cover letter refers to quarter ended March 31, 2025 while the call covers Q4 FY26 (March 31, 2026).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on results and the three-year doubling guidance, reaffirmed without qualification. Somewhat evasive on promoter stake plans and on co-lending timelines, which depend on bank confirmation.
key_quotes: We reported highest-ever quarterly profit after tax of Rs.722 million in Q4 FY26, up by 56% year-on-year, supported by strong income growth and improving operating leverage.
We typically follow a 50% to 60% LTV on the secured cases.
So the investor or the Company never suffers a principal loss or a cost of fund loss.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed doubling AUM, income and net profit over FY27-FY29 (~100% in three years, roughly 26% CAGR), with NIM held at ~6.5% in FY27; backing is partial, with 20 branch additions, six new lending segments and one SBI co-lending arrangement expected live in Q1 FY27, but no capex or capacity figures for the doubling.
